nodes.title: FET Phase
nodes.description: Further Education and Training Phase (Grades 10-12)

nodes.title: Physical Sciences
nodes.description: Physical Sciences — Grade 12 — CAPS Curriculum

nodes.title: Term 1
nodes.description: SBA: Control test

nodes.title: Mechanics: Momentum and Impulse
nodes.description: Newton's second law in terms of momentum; impulse; conservation of linear momentum; collisions.

nodes.title: Momentum definition and vector nature
nodes.description: Define momentum and calculate momentum using p = mv. Understand the vector nature of momentum.

nodes.title: Newton's second law in terms of momentum
nodes.description: Express Newton's second law as Fnet = dp/dt. Relate net force to change in momentum.

nodes.title: Impulse and impulse-momentum theorem
nodes.description: Define impulse as Fnet·Δt = mΔv. Apply the impulse-momentum theorem. Discuss safety applications (e.g. crumple zones, airbags).

nodes.title: Conservation of linear momentum and collisions
nodes.description: State and apply the law of conservation of linear momentum for isolated systems. Distinguish between elastic and inelastic collisions. Solve problems involving collisions and explosions.

nodes.title: Mechanics: Vertical Projectile Motion
nodes.description: Projectile motion in one dimension (vertical); equations of motion; graphical analysis.

nodes.title: Definition and equations of motion for vertical projectiles
nodes.description: Define a projectile. Use equations of motion to solve problems for objects in free fall, thrown vertically upward, thrown vertically downward, and bouncing objects.

nodes.title: Graphs of vertical projectile motion
nodes.description: Sketch and interpret position-time (x-t), velocity-time (v-t), and acceleration-time (a-t) graphs for free-falling objects, objects thrown upward, objects thrown downward, and bouncing objects. Derive position and velocity equations from graphs.

nodes.title: Matter and Materials: Organic Molecules
nodes.description: Functional groups; homologous series; IUPAC naming; structural isomers; physical properties; reactions of organic compounds.

nodes.title: Key definitions and terminology
nodes.description: Define: organic molecule, functional group, hydrocarbon, homologous series, saturated compound, unsaturated compound, structural isomer.

nodes.title: Homologous series: structures and formulae
nodes.description: Write condensed structural, structural (displayed), and molecular formulae (up to 8 carbon atoms) for: alkanes, alkenes, alkynes, alcohols, haloalkanes, carboxylic acids, aldehydes, ketones, and esters.

nodes.title: IUPAC nomenclature
nodes.description: Apply IUPAC rules to name and draw organic compounds including alkyl substituents. Name and draw structural isomers: chain isomers, positional isomers, and functional isomers.

nodes.title: Physical properties and intermolecular forces
nodes.description: Relate physical properties (melting point, boiling point, vapour pressure, viscosity, density, solubility) to intermolecular forces, functional group, chain length, and branching.

nodes.title: Reactions of organic compounds
nodes.description: Write equations for: combustion of alkanes; ester formation (condensation reaction); addition reactions (e.g. hydrogenation, halogenation, hydrohalogenation, hydration); elimination reactions (dehydrohalogenation, dehydration); substitution reactions (halogenation of alkanes, hydrolysis of halogenoalkanes).

nodes.title: Term 2
nodes.description: SBA: June examination or control test

nodes.title: Mechanics: Work, Energy and Power
nodes.description: Work done by a force; work-energy theorem; conservation of mechanical energy; power.

nodes.title: Work done by a force
nodes.description: Define work done by a force. Draw force and free-body diagrams. Calculate net work. Distinguish between positive and negative work.

nodes.title: Work-energy theorem
nodes.description: State and apply the work-energy theorem: net work done on an object equals the change in kinetic energy.

nodes.title: Conservation of mechanical energy and non-conservative forces
nodes.description: Distinguish between conservative and non-conservative forces. State and apply the conservation of mechanical energy. Apply Wnc = ΔEk + ΔEp to solve problems involving friction and other non-conservative forces.

nodes.title: Power
nodes.description: Define power as P = W/Δt. Calculate average power using Pave = Fvave. Determine minimum power required for pumping liquids.

nodes.title: Waves, Sound and Light: Doppler Effect
nodes.description: Doppler effect for sound; applications; red-shift and the expanding universe.

nodes.title: Doppler effect — concept and change in pitch
nodes.description: State the Doppler effect. Explain the change in observed pitch as a source moves towards or away from a listener.

nodes.title: Doppler calculations and applications
nodes.description: Solve problems using fL = ((v ± vL)/(v ± vs)) × fs. Describe applications such as ultrasound in medicine. Explain red-shift as evidence for the expanding universe.

nodes.title: Chemical Change: Rate and Extent of Reaction
nodes.description: Reaction rate; factors affecting rate; collision theory; activation energy.

nodes.title: Reaction rate definition and measurement
nodes.description: Define reaction rate. Calculate reaction rate from experimental data (change in concentration per unit time, or volume of gas produced per unit time).

nodes.title: Factors affecting reaction rate and collision theory
nodes.description: Explain how concentration, pressure, temperature, surface area, and catalysts affect reaction rate using collision theory. Interpret distribution of molecular energies (Maxwell-Boltzmann) graphs. Describe the role of a positive catalyst.

nodes.title: Chemical Change: Chemical Equilibrium
nodes.description: Dynamic equilibrium; Le Chatelier's principle; equilibrium constant Kc.

nodes.title: Open/closed systems and dynamic equilibrium
nodes.description: Distinguish between open and closed systems. Explain reversible reactions and dynamic equilibrium (forward rate = reverse rate, constant concentrations).

nodes.title: Le Chatelier's principle
nodes.description: State Le Chatelier's principle. Predict and explain shifts in equilibrium position due to changes in concentration, temperature, and pressure.

nodes.title: Equilibrium constant Kc
nodes.description: Write the expression for the equilibrium constant Kc. Perform calculations using Kc. Interpret the significance of high and low Kc values in terms of extent of reaction.

nodes.title: Chemical Change: Acids and Bases
nodes.description: Acid-base theories; strength and concentration; conjugate pairs; neutralisation; pH; Ka/Kb; titrations.

nodes.title: Acid-base definitions and strength
nodes.description: Compare Arrhenius and Lowry-Brønsted definitions. Distinguish strong from weak acids and bases, and concentrated from dilute. Identify conjugate acid-base pairs.

nodes.title: Neutralisation and titrations
nodes.description: Write neutralisation reaction equations. Perform volumetric calculations from titration data. Choose an appropriate indicator for a given titration.

nodes.title: pH scale, Kw, Ka and Kb
nodes.description: Define and calculate pH. Explain auto-ionisation of water and the ion product constant Kw. Calculate [H3O+] and [OH-] from pH. Use Ka and Kb values to compare relative strengths of acids and bases. Explain pH of salt solutions (hydrolysis).

nodes.title: Term 3
nodes.description: SBA: Trial examination (Paper 1 and Paper 2)

nodes.title: Electricity and Magnetism: Electric Circuits
nodes.description: Series and parallel circuits with internal resistance; emf and terminal potential difference.

nodes.title: Series and parallel circuits with internal resistance
nodes.description: Solve problems involving series and parallel circuits with up to four resistors excluding internal resistance. Apply emf = IR_ext + Ir. Distinguish emf from terminal potential difference.

nodes.title: Electrodynamics
nodes.description: Generators; motors; electromagnetic induction; AC vs DC; RMS values; average power.

nodes.title: Generators and electromagnetic induction
nodes.description: Explain how AC and DC generators work. Describe energy conversion in generators. State Faraday's law of electromagnetic induction. Identify components of AC and DC generators.

nodes.title: Motors and the motor effect
nodes.description: Explain how electric motors work. Describe the motor effect and identify the components of a motor. Compare advantages of AC and DC in transmission.

nodes.title: AC graphs, RMS values and average power
nodes.description: Interpret voltage-time (V-t) and current-time (I-t) graphs for AC. Calculate RMS values (Irms = Imax/√2; Vrms = Vmax/√2). Calculate average power using Pave = IrmsVrms = Irms²R = Vrms²/R.

nodes.title: Optical Phenomena and Properties of Materials
nodes.description: Photoelectric effect; work function; atomic emission and absorption spectra.

nodes.title: Photoelectric effect
nodes.description: Describe the photoelectric effect. Define threshold frequency and work function. Apply E = Wo + Ek(max). Explain the effect of intensity and frequency on photoelectron emission. Describe the particle nature of light (photons).

nodes.title: Atomic emission and absorption spectra
nodes.description: Explain the origin of atomic emission and absorption spectra in terms of electron energy level transitions. Interpret line spectra as evidence for quantised energy levels.

nodes.title: Electrochemical Reactions
nodes.description: Redox reactions; galvanic cells; standard electrode potentials; electrolytic cells.

nodes.title: Oxidation and reduction
nodes.description: Define oxidation and reduction in terms of electron transfer and change in oxidation number. Identify oxidising and reducing agents. Identify anode and cathode. Define electrolyte.

nodes.title: Galvanic cells
nodes.description: Describe the functioning of a galvanic cell (role of salt bridge, half-reactions, cell notation). Calculate cell emf using standard electrode potentials. Use the standard hydrogen electrode as reference. Predict how Vcell changes as reactants are consumed.

nodes.title: Electrolytic cells
nodes.description: Describe electrolysis of copper(II) chloride solution, electroplating, copper refining, and electrolysis of sodium chloride solution (chloro-alkali process). Write half-reactions and overall cell reactions for each process.

nodes.title: Trial Examination
nodes.description: Trial examination: Paper 1 (150 marks — Mechanics 65, Waves/Sound/Light 15, Electricity/Magnetism 55, Matter/Materials 15); Paper 2 (150 marks — Chemical Change 92, Matter/Materials 58).

nodes.title: Term 4
nodes.description: Revision and final NSC examination

nodes.title: Revision
nodes.description: Structured revision of all Grade 12 Physical Sciences content in preparation for the final NSC examination.

nodes.title: Final NSC Examination
nodes.description: Final NSC examination: Paper 1 (150 marks — Mechanics 65, Waves/Sound/Light 15, Electricity/Magnetism 55, Matter/Materials 15); Paper 2 (150 marks — Chemical Change 92, Matter/Materials 58).
